doc.title: David Torkanowsky interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, September 26, 2019

title: Accompanying singers: Dianne Reeves and Dave Bartholomew
summary: He discusses intimate accompaniment, great accompanists, rescuing Bartholomew's dropped beat on radio, and Dr. John's musicianship.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Okay. Speaking of human beings, singers, playing behind singers.
I was the pianist with Dianne Reeves for nine years.

And it’s a very, very intimate relationship. Like just when they’re singing out of time it’s like you start to learn to listen for the mouth opening because you know they’re about to go [sings] I — and you know where the down beat is. So it’s a very, you know the best that I’ve ever heard, besides Jimmy Rowles and the old guys, is Mulgrew Miller. He was so good, he was so good at it. Billy Childs was really great at it. You know there’s a lot of great accompanists. I was never on that level. But I could always intuit phrasing pretty well.
You had a little anecdote about on the radio thing playing behind David Bartholomew and he was playing “Body and Soul” and he — it sounded to me like maybe he dropped a beat here and there.

Well he definitely dropped a beat and you know, and the same thing with singers. It’s not about being right and wrong, you make whatever — no. Your role as an accompanist is to justify what happens. You’re accompanying them. And just because they may have gotten a point off on their musicology final exam doesn’t mean that you leave them out to dry, and especially a griot, an icon as Dave Bartholomew. But Dr. John called me up at the radio station, “Yeah I heard what you did bro, that was nice.”
You caught that, you fixed that.

Now I’ll say this though as an aside. Dr. John could play Bill Evans’ tunes. He was a musician of the highest order. When you hear Dr. John play “Waltz for Debbie” it’s like transformative. But obviously he wasn’t known for that, but he was a good musician. Sorry you were going to —
